title: Sultanate of Banten
capsule: The Banten Sultanate was founded in northwest Java c. 1526–1527 when the Muslim leader Sunan Gunungjati and his forces defeated the Hindu Sunda kingdom's port of Banten, establishing an Islamic trading polity. Under Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa (r. 1651–1683) the sultanate reached its greatest power, controlling west Java and parts of Sumatra and becoming a major pepper exporter attracting English and Danish as well as Dutch traders. Internal conflict between Sultan Ageng and his son Sultan Haji enabled the VOC to intervene; Ageng was captured in 1683 and Banten became a Dutch client. The VOC formally abolished the sultanate in 1808, integrating its territories into the colonial Batavian Republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's core territory in northwest Java is well attested; its claimed suzerainty over parts of Sumatra and the Lampung region is variably documented.
